beats.text: Now a quick diagnostic. Here are six statements. Decide whether each is correct, and if not, name the trap. Pause and decide.

One: wrong. Convert seventy-five point zero millilitres to litres, giving zero point zero six zero zero moles. Two: wrong. Use only the reacting component's share of the mixture. Three: wrong. Only twenty-one percent of air is oxygen. Four: wrong. Divide by the limiting reactant, the one that actually reacts, not the one in excess. Five: wrong. Joules per degree times degrees gives joules, not kilojoules. Six: correct.

Seven: wrong. The highest reading underestimates the rise when heat is being lost, so extrapolate the cooling line. Eight: wrong. Close agreement shows precision, but a systematic error can shift every repeat. Nine: wrong. A catalyst lowers the activation energy but doesn't change delta H. Ten: correct. Eleven: wrong. Per mole of fuel isn't per useful kilojoule; the energy released and the efficiency matter too. Twelve: wrong. A renewable fuel can still compete with food, use a lot of water, or leak methane. Add any you missed to your error log.
